title: lsp
summary: Starts the LSP (Language Server Protocol) stdio server
intro: Read this when you want hover, completion, go-to-definition and diagnostics in an editor other than RAD Studio. It starts the language server over stdio; the IDE plugin launches it by itself, and it is not the same as the MCP server (serve) used by AI clients.

help: drag-lint lsp                --db <file.sqlite>    (LSP stdio server) [--stdio] [--parent-pid <n>] [--clientProcessId <n>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>]
--stdio and --clientProcessId are accepted and IGNORED -- editor clients pass them;
stdio is the only transport, and --parent-pid is the shutdown watch that DOES act.
in lsp mode the engine also listens on a per-user maintenance pipe -- see `drag-lint shutdown`.

--proxy [--delphi-lsp <path>] [--trace <file>] [--merge-diagnostics] [--merge-completion] [--merge-hover] [--merge-definition] [--merge-budget-ms <n>] [--delphi-lsp-bits 32|64]: relay in front of RAD Studio's DelphiLSP,
so registering drag-lint as the Code Insight server keeps the compiler front end.
--trace appends every relayed LSP message to <file> with a direction tag (C>S / S>C); off by default.
--merge-diagnostics: append drag-lint's lint findings to DelphiLSP's publishDiagnostics (one notification, source-tagged); OFF by default.
--merge-completion: union drag-lint's completion items into DelphiLSP's reply, keyed on (label, kind); DelphiLSP's items first; OFF by default.
--merge-hover: append drag-lint's hover facts to DelphiLSP's hover after a --- rule, or answer with them alone when DelphiLSP has none; OFF by default.
--merge-definition: drag-lint's definition when DelphiLSP's is null or empty; answer references and workspace/symbol in the proxy (DelphiLSP has neither); OFF by default.
--merge-budget-ms <n>: per-frame budget for a merge handler; over budget forwards DelphiLSP's bytes untouched (default 300).
--delphi-lsp-bits 32|64: which DelphiLSP the proxy spawns (64 = bin64\DelphiLSP.exe, the default; 32 = bin\DelphiLSP.exe); --delphi-lsp <path> wins over it.
--full-rules: run the FULL rule set (built-ins included) out-of-process on every didSave and publish the complete finding set; OFF by default -- costs one `lint` run per save, reported on stderr.
drag-lint index <dir> --db <file.sqlite> --resolve-only   (re-derive call edges / ancestry / helpers / purity verdicts from the STORED parses; skips the walk entirely --
the cheap remedy when resolver_fingerprint says the edges are stale, since no parse became wrong)
it writes edges INSIDE this one index only -- no cross-store edges are written (measured
2026-09-22: 0 refs.external_target in every project DB; re-resolving the libraries under
resolver 1.5.1 added 13 intra-library edges per platform, and nothing across stores)
drag-lint index --project <file.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> --resolve-only   (the same, for a PROJECT database -- the form
to type there: without --resolve-only the <dir> form above widens a project DB into a folder DB)
drag-lint index --all --resolve-only   (the same, across every manifest section -- the only command that reaches them all;
use it to repair indexes stamped by a build that skipped the pass, which no later build can detect)

library-first resolve: a section with libraryResolve whose platform library is not READY (missing, rebuilding, stale extractor) is resolved without it; the run marks the DB pending (schema_meta library_resolve_state) and says on stderr that the result is INCOMPLETE. The next index run re-resolves it once the library is ready, no flag needed.

questions.ask: How do I start the language server for another editor?
